newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil publishes drafts of pay-tv tender papers.
newsitem.headline: Brazil publishes drafts of pay-tv tender papers.

text.p: Brazil's Communications Ministry took a step closer to tendering out new pay-television concessions Tuesday when it published rough drafts of bid specification documents.
The documents will be open for consultations for 20 days, according to a notice in the government's daily gazette.
"We expect that bidding for a first concession will begin in late August," a Communications Ministry spokesman said.
Brazil is seeking to tender out about 1,500 concessions to private groups who will provide cable television and high-frequency multi-point distribution services (MMDS).
The concessions will be for 15 years, renewable for further 15-year periods.
Groups providing cable television services would have to be at least 51 percent Brazilian-owned while providers of MMDS would have to be based in the country, the regulations said.
